newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firms on Chinese demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firms on Chinese demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps extend its recent rise at midday Friday supported by regional demand and firmer overnight crude and product prices in the west, market sources said.
"The market has rebounded with demand seen from China and supplies in Singapore are tight," one trader said.

January gas oil swaps traded this morning at $30.50 and $30.75 a barrel, up about 50 cents from Thursday, brokers said. The market was last quoted at $30.90/$31.00, they said. Last Friday, January paper traded at a five-year record of $33.07.
Overnight January Brent crude on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) gained 37 cents a barrel to close at $22.52 while December gas oil futures was up $2.25 a tonne to end at $207.00.

Demand was also seen for jet fuel from North Asia which led to higher premiums. A Japanese refiner earlier this week bought a 30,000-tonne cargo for arrival in the second half of January at about $2.30 a barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f basis.
The last deal was done at a $1.80-premium.
But Jet swaps prices were notionally unchanged in very thin trade with some brokers expecting bids to improve later Friday as activity picks up.
January jet fuel/gas oil swap spread or regrade was bid at $1.50 a barrel.
Fuel oil was quoted unchanged January at $118.50/$119.75.
